design_decisions.decision: hal_button_is_pressed() is a raw, instantaneous GPIO level read -- no debounce, no edge-detection, no 'trusted event' semantics of its own.
design_decisions.why: commissioning_window.hpp's own header already establishes the precedent this project follows for this exact situation: 'a caller with a real button interrupt/task would call commissioning_window_start() with kTrustedButtonAction once it has one' -- that caller/task does not exist yet for either grant, so building debounce logic now, with nothing real driving it, would be speculative. The HAL's contract is deliberately narrow and honest: 'is the pin low right now', nothing more.

design_decisions.decision: GPIO9 (the real ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1 BOOT button) as the Kconfig default, confirmed via Espressif's own official user-guide documentation before writing any code, not assumed from general ESP32 convention.
design_decisions.why: This project's own established discipline: ground every hardware fact against a real source, not memory. WebSearch confirmed GPIO9 is a strapping pin only during power-up/reset and is safely readable as an ordinary active-low input afterward -- both facts this design depends on. SOC_GPIO_PIN_COUNT=31 for ESP32-C6 (checked in the real espressif/idf:release-v5.5 image's soc_caps.h) grounds the Kconfig range 0-30, not an arbitrary bound.

design_decisions.decision: PhysicalPresenceGrantState is bound to all three dimensions plan #21 names (boot, session, action class) simultaneously, not just one or two.
design_decisions.why: Read literally: 'is bound to gateway boot/session/action class' -- boot binding is free (RAM-only storage, same trick session_store.hpp/commissioning_window.hpp already use), session binding is an explicit char[] compare (empty/null on both sides counts as a deliberate 'not session-scoped' match, not a bypass), action-class binding is an explicit enum compare. All three must hold for physical_presence_grant_is_valid()/_consume() to succeed.

design_decisions.decision: A second physical_presence_grant_create() call REPLACES rather than rejects an already-active grant.
design_decisions.why: The plan names no 'already active' error case for this grant, exactly the same textual gap commissioning_window_start()'s own doc comment already identified and resolved the same way for its own analogous case -- consistency with an established, already-user-facing precedent in the same codebase, not a new judgment call invented from nothing.
